GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2015-01-31T19:06:04Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Different rules for function parameter compatibility when assignment is on a different line to variable declaration.
Description: A function can choose to omit parameters defined in a signature, as shown by function `a` below. Callers of `a` must still supply arguments, but the function does not need to use them.

Despite this, if the same function is assigned later in the program, this no longer applies and the identical function is now not compatible, as shown with function `b`.

``` typescript
interface X {
    (source: number): boolean;
}

var a: X = function() { return true; }

var b: X;
// Why is this an error?
var b = function() { return true; }
```

Shouldn't both of these cases follow the same rules?
